title: FP8 numeric sentinel and autocorrector for E4M3/E5M2 on Hopper
creator: Maria Chen
description: Problem: Enabling FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) on Hopper shows sporadic numeric instability on tail-of-distribution inputs and long-context workloads. Root causes seem tied to per-op dynamic range misestimation and cross-shard KV cache amplification. Goal: implement a lightweight runtime "numeric sentinel" that detects small but meaningful drift in output distributions and triggers an automatic corrective path (per-op scaling adjustment or transparent fallback to an INT8/FP16 variant) before customers observe quality regressions. This ticket scopes the sentinel design, telemetry, localized autotune, regression tests, and a controlled rollout strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel emits a per-request numeric-stability signal that is ingestible by our observability pipeline (logs + metrics).
When sentinel thresholds exceed configured tolerances, runtime performs one of: (a) per-op scale adjust and retry, (b) route to pre-quantized INT8 variant, with fallback decision within 250ms.
Golden-suite accuracy regression tests (1000 prompts across intents) show <0.5% QA delta vs FP16 baseline after autocorrector enabled for E4M3/E5M2 on latest hopper image.
Canary rollout to 2% of traffic in us-west-2 with automatic rollback if customer-facing error-rate or perplexity drift crosses thresholds documented in release runbook.
Documentation (Confluence + runtime config reference) and a post-deploy monitoring dashboard are published.
implementation_notes: Sentinel signals: token-level KL divergence approx, per-op outlier ratio, per-shard histogram shift, and inference runtime NaN/inf counters.

Local autocorrector: perform a fast per-op scale tweak (multiply scale by 1.05 or 0.95 depending on sign) and retry the offending op up to 2 times. If instability persists, transparently route request to INT8/FP16 variant on same model version.
Telemetry: add metric quant.sentinel_trips, quant.sentinel_mode (scale_adjust|fallback), quant.sentinel_latency_ms, and tags: model, shard, op_type, region.
Runtime hooks: small hot-path in serving runtime avoiding heap allocations; use preallocated scratch buffers and non-blocking retry path to keep P99 latency SLAs stable.
Safety: damping to prevent oscillation (minimum 1 minute cooldown per shard), and global kill-switch via feature flag for emergency rollback.
Calibration: augment nightly calibration job to surface ops with high sentinel activation counts; feed back into per-op quant profiles for future releases.
